title: Legislative definition — the term pinned to its definition
titleEs: Definición legislativa — Microescena con objetos y actores
description: Top-down reading desk: a hand lens finds and marks a term in an article extract; the other hand opens the full text at the index flag of the level that holds the definitions section; two pins and a cord join the term to the entry that supplies its definition, which lights up only once the pin is in. Fictional text, user-supplied hierarchy, supplied state only.

content.note: Visual illustration only. It does not state the law of any jurisdiction or decide validity, responsibility or outcomes.

license: Original vector artwork and code created for this project; no third-party assets.

durationMs.description: Total length of the finite timeline in milliseconds. Phases scale proportionally; the final state is held.

seed.description: Seed for small deterministic variations (appearance defaults, hand-drawn jitter). Same seed + time + params = same frame.

locale.description: Language of built-in labels (en or es). User-supplied text is never translated.

theme.description: Render treatment. Only tested themes are listed.

palette.description: Colour palette applied to props, actors and accents.

background.description: transparent, paper, white, light-grey, charcoal or a #rrggbb colour.

safeArea.description: Caption-safe margins as fractions of the frame.

reducedMotion.description: Removes decorative motion (overshoot, idle sway, camera drift) while keeping instructional motion.

textVisibility.description: all labels, key labels only, or none (the action must remain readable without labels).

jurisdiction.description: Descriptive jurisdiction tag. "unspecified" means no legal system is asserted.

contentNotice.description: Shows a small "illustrative example" tag inside the safe area.

sources.description: Fictional source names: [0] is printed on the book (the full text that holds both sections); [1] names the separate note in which an ordinary use is proposed (scenes that show it) (array replaces the previous value)

hierarchy.description: User-supplied ordering of the divisions of the text, drawn top to bottom as index flags on the book. The order is the author's; the scene implies no rule of precedence between levels (array replaces the previous value)

ref.description: Reference printed on the page, e.g. "Text 1 · Art. 7 (fictional)"

text.description: Simulated wording: for [0] the clause that uses the term; for [1] the definition wording that follows the term

term.description: The term as written in this passage

level.description: Hierarchy level (1 = first flag) that holds the passage

passages.description: Fictional passages: [0] the article in which the term is USED; [1] the section that SUPPLIES the definition (array replaces the previous value)

entryRow.description: Row of the definitions page (1–3) that holds the supplied definition

b.description: Caption for the article extract (the object the term comes from)

actorLabels.description: Role captions shown next to each actor

hierarchy.description: Caption above the index flags (the user-supplied hierarchy)

actionProgress.description: How far the concrete action is allowed to progress (1 = complete; lower values freeze it part-way)

target.description: Scene element the annotation points at

items.description: Editorial annotation shown during the hold

annotations.description: Editorial callouts shown in the final hold (array replaces the previous value)

finalState.description: Supplied state held at the end: definition-linked (cord from the term to the definition), definition-located (book opened at the definitions, no link), term-marked (only the term is marked). No legal conclusion is inferred.

passages.heading: Keeping of items
passages.text: The holder keeps each listed item in the register (simulated wording).
